translations.text: But the men of that place were Benjaminites.
The old man looked up and saw the travelers in the streets of the city. The old man said, "Where are you coming from, and where are you going?"

He said to him, "We are coming from Bethlehem in Judah, and we are going to the hill country of Ephraim. I am from there. I had gone to Bethlehem in Judah, and now I am going home. But no one will take us into his house and give me lodging.
We have straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine for ourselves, for your maidservant, for this young man, and for your servants. We lack nothing that we need."
The old man said to them, "Peace be with you! If you lack anything, let it be my concern. Only do not stay in the streets."
He brought them into his house and gave fodder to their donkeys. He washed their feet, and they ate and drank.

While they were enjoying themselves, the men of that city, wicked men, surrounded his house and beat on his door. They spoke to the old man, the master of the house, and said, "Bring out the man who came into your house, so that we may know him."
The man, the master of the house, went out and said to them, "No, do not do anything evil at all. This man has come into my house. Do not do this foolish thing!
Here are my virgin daughter and his concubine. I will bring them out to you. Humble them and do to them whatever seems good in your eyes. But do not do this foolish thing to the man."

But they would not listen to him. So the man took hold of his wife and brought her out to them. They knew her and humbled her all night until morning. They abused her, and they let her go only when dawn was breaking.
At daybreak the woman came and fell down at the door of the house where her husband was, and she gave up her spirit.
In the morning her husband got up, opened the doors of the house, and went outside to go on his way. And there was the woman, his wife, fallen in the road, with her hands lying in front of the door.
He said to her, "Get up, and let us go." But she gave him no answer, for she was dead. He picked her up and put her on the donkey, and the man went to his home.
He took a sword, took hold of his wife, and cut her limb by limb into twelve pieces. He sent them to all the tribes of Israel.

Everyone who saw it said, "Nothing like this has ever happened, and no one has ever seen such a thing, from the time the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt until now. Now take counsel about this and say what we should do."
All the Israelites came out, and the assembly gathered as one man, from Dan to Beersheba, along with the land of Gilead, and they came to the Lord at Mizpah.
All the people and all the tribes of Israel stood together in one place: the assembly of God, four hundred thousand foot soldiers armed with swords.
The Benjaminites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. The Israelites said, "Tell us, where did this great evil happen?"
The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered and said: "My concubine and I came to Gibeah of Benjamin to lodge for the night.
And the men of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house I was in at night. They meant to kill me, and they humbled my wife; they abused her, and she died.
And I took hold of her and cut her up limb by limb, and I sent her to all the territories of Israel. For they have done this great evil in Israel.
And now, here you all are, sons of Israel: give your word and counsel about them."
And all the people rose up as one man and said: "None of us will go to his dwelling, and none of us will turn back to his house.
And now this is what we will do to Gibeah: we will go up against it by casting lots.

And we will take ten men out of every hundred, a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to bring provisions for the people, so that they may carry out the deed — those who go into Gibeah of Benjamin — on account of all the folly that they have done in Israel."
And all the people of Israel, who had come from the cities, gathered at the city as one man.
And the tribes of Israel sent to the sons of Benjamin and said: "What is this wickedness that has been done among you?

Now hand over to us those godless men of Gibeah, and we will put them to death and remove this wickedness from Israel." But the sons of Benjamin would not listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.
And the sons of Benjamin gathered from their cities at Gibeah, to go out and fight the sons of Israel.

And on that day the sons of Benjamin who had come from the cities were mustered, and they were about twenty-five thousand sword-bearing men, all warriors, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were also counted, and they were seven hundred,
chosen men out of all the people, who could use both hands as their right. All of these were slingers, who could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
And all the men of Israel, apart from the sons of Benjamin, were mustered, and they were four hundred thousand sword-bearing men, all of them warriors.

And they rose up and went up to Bethel and inquired of God, and the sons of Israel said: "Who shall go up first as our leader to fight the sons of Benjamin?" And the Lord said: "Judah shall go up first as leader."
And the sons of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped near Gibeah.
And the men of Israel went out to fight Benjamin, and the men of Israel drew up in battle order against Gibeah.
And the sons of Benjamin came out of the city and on that day destroyed twenty-two thousand of the men of Israel on the spot.
And the sons of Israel took courage and again drew up in battle order in the same place where they had drawn up on the first day.

And the sons of Israel came and wept before the Lord until evening. Then they inquired of God and said: "Shall we again draw near to fight Benjamin, our brother?" And the Lord said: "Go up against him."
And the sons of Israel advanced against the sons of Benjamin on the second day.
And Benjamin rushed out of Gibeah to meet them in battle on the second day, and struck down eighteen thousand men of the people of Israel on the spot, all of them men who drew the sword.
And the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel, and they wept before the Lord and fasted on that day. And they offered peace offerings.
And the ark of the covenant of the Lord God was there in those days.

And Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, stood before him in those days. And the sons of Israel inquired of the Lord and said: "Shall we go out yet again to battle against Benjamin our brother, or shall we stop?" And the Lord said to them: "Tomorrow I will give them into your hands."
And the sons of Israel set an ambush around Gibeah.
And the sons of Israel went up against Benjamin on the third day and drew up in battle order before Gibeah, as they had the first and second time.

And the sons of Benjamin came out to battle against the people, and they were drawn away from the city. They began to strike down some of the people and wound them, as before, on the roads, one of which goes up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah, in the field. And about thirty men of Israel fell.
And the sons of Benjamin said: "They are falling before us as they did at first." But the sons of Israel said: "Let us flee and draw them away from the city onto the roads." And they did so.
And all the men of Israel rose from their place and drew up in battle order at Baal-tamar. And the ambush of Israel attacked at the places to the west of Gibeah.
And they came before Gibeah, ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and the battle grew heavy upon them. And they did not know that disaster had come upon them,
and the Lord struck Benjamin down before Israel. On that day the sons of Israel killed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin, all of them men who drew the sword.
And Benjamin saw that he was defeated. And the men of Israel gave ground to Benjamin, because they were relying on the ambush that they had set around Gibeah.
And the ambush rushed forward and spread out into Gibeah. They went in and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.
And the men of Israel had agreed with the ambush, with the sword [?], that a fire and smoke would be raised in the city.
And the men of Israel turned to fight Benjamin. Benjamin had only begun to strike down and wound the men of Israel, about thirty men, for they said: "They are surely fleeing before us, as at first."
And the signal, the pillar of smoke, rose up above the city. And Benjamin looked behind him, and behold, smoke was rising from the city to heaven.
And the sons of Israel turned back. And the sons of Benjamin hurried and fled before the sons of Israel when they saw that disaster had come upon them,
and they turned onto the road to the wilderness. But the fighters caught up with them, and those who were in the city were killing them in their midst.
And they struck down the sons of Benjamin. And they pursued them from Nohah onward, close on their track, as far as the front of Gibeah, toward the sunrise.
And eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all of them mighty men.

And the survivors looked back and fled into the wilderness toward the rock of Rimmon. And on the roads they killed five thousand more men. And they pursued close behind them as far as Gibeah, and killed two thousand more men of them.
And all the men of Benjamin who fell on that day were fifty-five thousand, men who bore the sword, all of them mighty warriors.
And the survivors turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, for four months.

And the sons of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin and destroyed them with the edge of the sword, from the city onward, down to the livestock. And everything that was found in the cities, and all the cities that were left, they burned with fire.
And the men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah on that day, saying: "None of us shall give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife."
And the people went out and came to Bethel, and they sat there before the Lord until evening. And they raised their voices and wept bitterly,
and they said: "O Lord God of Israel, why has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be wiped out from Israel?"
And on the next day the people rose early, built an altar, and offered the sacrifice of salvation.

And the sons of Israel said: "Who out of all the tribes of Israel did not come up to the Lord, to this assembly?" For a great oath had been made about anyone who did not come to the Lord at Mizpah, and they had said: "He shall surely be put to death!"
And the sons of Israel grieved over their brother Benjamin, and said: "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.
What shall we do for those who are left without wives? For we have sworn by the Lord that we will not give them any of our daughters as wives."
And they said: "Which one tribe of the people of Israel did not come up to the Lord at Mizpah?" And not one man from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp, to that assembly.
And the people were counted, and not one man of the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead was there.
And the people sent twelve thousand of the mighty men there, and commanded them, saying: "Go and destroy all the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword, the women and their people."
"And this is what you shall do: every male, and every woman who has lain with a man, you shall put under the ban, but the virgins you shall spare." And they did so.
And among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead they found four hundred young virgins who had not lain with a man, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the city of Canaan.
And the whole assembly sent word and spoke to the sons of Benjamin who were at the rock of Rimmon, and offered them peace.
And Benjamin returned to the sons of Israel at that time, and they gave them as wives the women of Jabesh-gilead, and this pleased them.
And the people grieved over Benjamin, for the Lord did not make a breach among the tribes of Israel.
And the elders of the assembly said: "What shall we do for these remaining men who are left without wives, since the women of Benjamin have been wiped out?"
And they said: "There must be an inheritance for the surviving remnant of Benjamin, so that a tribe is not wiped out from Israel.
But we cannot give them wives from our daughters, for we sons of Israel have sworn, saying: 'Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin!'"
And they said: "Look, every year there is a feast of the Lord at Shiloh, which lies north of Bethel, east of the [?] that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."
And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying: "Go and lie in wait in the vineyards."

And watch: when the daughters of the inhabitants of Shiloh come out dancing in the dances, then come out and seize, each of you, a wife for himself from the daughters of Shiloh, and carry them off and go away to the land of Benjamin.

And when their fathers or their brothers come to bring a complaint against you, you shall say to them: "Have mercy on them, for no man took his wife in battle; nor did you give them to them, and so you have committed no guilt."

And they did so. And the sons of Benjamin took wives according to their number from the dancers whom they had seized, and they went away and returned to their inheritance, and rebuilt the cities and lived in them.
And at that time the sons of Israel departed from there, and each man went to his own tribe, and each man returned to his own inheritance.
In those days there was no king in Israel, and each man did what was right in his own eyes.
